title: Rectangular plate
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. This ensures that the part is aligned with the global coordinate system. Next, draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Begin with the first loop, drawing the first line from the origin at (0.0, 0.0) to (0.1406, 0.0), then the second line from (0.1406, 0.0) to (0.1406, 0.75), followed by the third line from (0.1406, 0.75) to (0.0, 0.75), and finally the fourth line from (0.0, 0.75) back to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to reduce its size proportionally. Since the Euler angles and translation vector are already set to zero, no additional transformations are necessary. To transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional model, extrude the sketch 0.0141 units along the normal direction. Ensure that the extrusion only occurs in one direction to create a solid body. The resulting part, named the rectangular plate, has a length of 0.140625 units, a width of 0.75 units, and a height of 0.0140625 units. The edges of the plate are rounded, and the surface is flat.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.1406, 0).lineTo(0.1406, 0.75).lineTo(0, 0.75).close()

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0141)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation (if needed)
# In this case, the coordinate system is the default (0, 0, 0) with no rotation, so no transformation is needed.

# Final model
r = extrusion

# Display the model

lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1406, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1406, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0141)
